en.title: Adjacent Digit Sum Encryption
en.description:
In each round, take the sum of every two adjacent digits modulo 10 to get a new array whose length is 1 less. Repeat until 2 digits remain, then output the string formed by those two digits, keeping leading zeros.

The standard input format, examples and test data were written independently by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n (2..100000); the second line contains n digits (0..9).
en.output: Output one integer, the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: [4,5,6,7] first becomes [9,1,3], then [0,4], so the output is 04; the leading zero must not be dropped. Example 2: two digits already remain, so output 00 directly. Example 3: the adjacent sums 9+1 and 1+9 are both 0 modulo 10, so output 00.
hints: Each of the final two digits is a weighted sum of a stretch of adjacent digits with the binomial coefficients of row n−2. Use Lucas's theorem to compute modulo 2 and modulo 5 separately, then combine them into modulo 10.
